tagline: Up the Arkansas and over Raton Pass on the wagons' road.
intro: In Colorado the byway follows the Arkansas River west by Lamar and La Junta to Bent's Old Fort, then cuts southwest across the prairie to Trinidad and over Raton Pass, 7,834 feet, into New Mexico. There it has two forks, as the trail did. The Mountain Branch runs south through Cimarron, the Cimarron Cutoff comes west from Clayton past the Rabbit Ear Mountains to Wagon Mound, and the two meet at Watrous for the last miles into Santa Fe.
The caravans ran for nearly sixty years, until the railroad reached Santa Fe in 1880. On a clear spring day a sharp eye can still find their ruts in the prairie.

moments.title: Bent's Old Fort
moments.text: An adobe trading post of 1833, where the Bents traded with the Cheyenne and Arapaho for buffalo robes and Kit Carson hunted for the company. It was rebuilt in 1976.

moments.title: St. James Hotel, Cimarron
moments.text: When the owner's sons replaced the roof in 1901 they found many bullet holes. A double layer of hardwood had kept the upstairs guests alive, and the dining room ceiling still shows about twenty.

moments.title: Fort Union
moments.text: The remains of three forts built from the 1850s on, and from the road in, the ruts of both the Mountain Branch and the Cimarron Branch of the trail.
